metadata.description: Single-plugin marketplace exposing the cc-enforcer discipline plugin.

plugins.name: cc-enforcer
plugins.description: Rules your coding agent physically cannot ignore. A Claude Code plugin (and LLM-agnostic rule pack) that stops reactive patching, guessed citations, surface-level fixes and premature "done" claims by intercepting the agent's own tool calls rather than asking it nicely. PreToolUse denies an edit before it lands — editing a file you never opened this session, a suppression marker with no adjacent why-comment, a hardcoded secret or user-home path, the fourth small patch to one file, a dangerous shell flag. A nine-layer Stop gate then refuses to let a completion claim end the turn without evidence, a convergence self-quiz, a fidelity check against the user's ORIGINAL request, and a one-line TL;DR. Twelve rules, ten backed by a hook; "Imperial Edict" regexes you define per project; a repo-wide sync gate; CI drift gates that derive every documented number from the code so the documentation cannot rot. Zero dependencies, stdlib only, Linux + Windows CI, and every guard fails OPEN — a bug in the discipline can never brick your agent. v0.39.1 is a documentation release with one gate behind it, and the gate's first finding closed. Pinning only the newest CHANGELOG heading against plugin.json answers the bump-vs-entry question and nothing else: the headings under it are unchecked, so a release that got its entry and its release: commit while the tag was never cut sat in the file with every gate green. tests/test_version_sync.py now compares the whole released set against git tag, and the first thing it named was this repository's own 0.38.2 — a heading and a release: commit with no tag underneath them, so there was nothing to install at that point in history, gh release view answered 'release not found', and the repository front page kept naming an older version as Latest. Closing it was a release-time action rather than a code change: v0.38.2 is now an annotated tag on its release commit carrying a GitHub release built from its own entry, so v0.38.1 -> v0.38.2 -> v0.38.3 is a complete sequence and the gate is green on the fact rather than on a waiver. Two versions are excused, and only because their own entries say so where readers see it: 0.8.0 was rolled into the v0.9.0 commit, and 0.25.1 was released inside the v0.26.0 commit that also wrote its heading. UNTAGGED_BY_RECORD registers them, a companion test re-derives that declaration from the CHANGELOG entry itself, and the registration has to end the day a tag appears — the registry cannot excuse a version the record has not admitted in public. CI checks out with fetch-depth: 0, because the default depth-1 checkout brings no tags and the gate would have nothing to read; the suite reads that line out of the workflow, since a shallow clone makes the tag check skip itself and would otherwise let a green run stand over a gate that inspected nothing. Both plugin descriptions and both READMEs were aligned with the code in the same pass: twelve rules with ten backed by a hook, and four CI drift gates, the demo gate named beside the version, doc and i18n ones. 742 -> 746 tests. Prior — v0.39.0 thins the injected contract, because it had been eating the feature it was supposed to leave room for. v0.38.3 fixed the symptom — edicts dropped silently on a long install path; this is the cause. The SessionStart contract had grown to 9,262 characters against a 10,000-character hook cap and nothing gated it: 991 characters of headroom at v0.29, 914 at v0.32, 552 at v0.35, by which point a real install path plus two real edicts no longer fit and a headline feature was degrading to nothing in the field. It is now 6,627 characters with 3,373 of headroom. What came out was duplication, not text: section 2's Recovery column, every word of which is printed at deny time in the block reason's own recovery section, and section 1's paragraph rows, whose heading already calls it a one-line index — each concept checked against prompts/user-prompt.md, re-injected EVERY turn, before being cut. Three tokens that lived only in the Recovery column were folded into the trigger cells rather than dropped. Three things the first pass cut that lived nowhere else at cold start went back in, caught by the tests that assert them: the four self-quiz questions verbatim and the layer (e) / layer (f) consequence for rules 08 and 09. The zh mirror got the same treatment, because a mirror that stops mirroring is how the deny set came to differ between languages in v0.26. The gate: a 120-character install root plus three edicts rendered by the real renderer must survive in both languages with no elision — ordinary parameters, named in the test, verified RED against the pre-thinning contract. 741 -> 742 tests (v0.39.0). Prior — v0.38.3 fixes two defects found by verifying v0.38.2 the way it should be verified — cloning the remote into a fresh directory and running the suite there. Five tests failed while CI was green on the same commit on two platforms, which made 'verification artefact' the obvious conclusion; both were real. The clone sat at a 110-character path and this repository lives at a 23-character one. First: when the contract alone fills the 10,000-character hook cap, build_context dropped every edict and returned SILENTLY, so a session on a deeply-nested install was governed by rules it had never been shown and had no way to learn about — the v0.34.1 defect (all edicts elided, notice reporting 0) living in the sibling branch three releases after the class was supposedly closed. Reproduced first-party across install-root lengths before the fix; the branch now reports the count using the same counter _clip_edicts locates cut points with, because counting twice two ways is how the original notice came to disagree with its own clipper. Second: the header printed the install root twice, and the second copy came out of the budget the header exists to protect — naming it once takes a 300-character root from losing every edict to keeping them. Also a test that sliced the first 200 characters and asserted a filename was inside: true at a 23-character root, false at 110, so it failed on code that was working. It measures the header now. Both fixes verified RED against the pre-fix code, the elision fix with a twin so it cannot degenerate into 'always drop everything and report it'. 738 -> 741 tests (v0.38.3). Full release history: CHANGELOG.md.
